c.tagline: Japan's cosmopolitan port city, where a futuristic bay skyline meets the country's largest Chinatown.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are strictly metered starting around ¥500; street hailing is common and reliable. Doors open automatically, and tipping is not expected.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance/medical emergencies. English-speaking operators may be limited; the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers 24/7 multilingual support.

avoid.reason: In the Noge and Fukutomicho bar districts late at night, avoid touts and check bar prices before ordering; otherwise very safe.

hood_desc: Yokohama's gleaming waterfront district of skyscrapers, the Landmark Tower, Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel, and Cup Noodles Museum; best for first-timers wanting modern sights, malls, and bay views all walkable.

The historic core around Kannai and Chinatown (Chukagai), home to Japan's largest Chinatown with hundreds of restaurants and temples plus the ballpark and old civic buildings; suits foodies and culture-seekers.

Elegant Motomachi shopping street below the leafy Yamate (Bluff) hillside of Western-style former foreign residences and the Harbour View Park; good for boutique shopping, cafes, and strolls with history.
The bustling commercial hub around Yokohama Station's west side, packed with department stores, restaurants, and nightlife; a convenient, well-connected base for transit across the city and to Tokyo.
The transit gateway around Shin-Yokohama Station with the Shinkansen stop, Nissan Stadium, and the Ramen Museum; a practical, quieter business-oriented area for onward bullet-train travel.

water.note: Tap water is treated to strict national standards and safe to drink directly.

transit.hours: Trains and subways run from roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; there is no all-night service, so late-night travel relies on taxis.
transit.note: Yokohama is served by JR lines, private railways (Keikyu, Tokyu, Sotetsu), the Minatomirai Line, and the Yokohama Municipal Subway (Blue and Green lines), with the Sea Bass ferry linking waterfront stops.
transit.pay: A rechargeable Suica or PASMO IC card (also on smartphones) works across all trains, subways, and buses; single paper tickets and contactless credit cards are also accepted on many lines.

ferry: Sea Bass waterfront ferry (Yokohama Station - Minato Mirai - Yamashita Park)
train: JR lines, Keikyu, Tokyu, Sotetsu, Minatomirai Line, Yokohama Municipal Subway

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus from Haneda (HND) to Yokohama City Air Terminal (YCAT) near Yokohama Station (~30 min)
Keikyu Airport Line train from Haneda to Yokohama Station (~25 min)
Narita Express (N'EX) or Airport Limousine Bus from Narita (NRT) to Yokohama (~90 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary anywhere in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is standard and included in the price.
